newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New tax delays St Petersburg's planned Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: New tax delays St Petersburg's planned Eurobond.

text.p: The City of St Petersburg is postponing its planned Eurobond because of uncertainty about a new tax on government securities, a senior municipal official said on Thursday.

Igor Artemyev, chairman of the city's finance committee, told a news conference that St Petersburg had had every chance of issuing the bond at the end of this month or early in February -- the time-frame outlined by officials this week.

But the introduction of a 15 percent tax on earnings on government securities had created additional risks. The city was therefore postponing the issue until it was able to study full details of the tax.

"Until foreign investors sort out what is happening with this tax, especially if they buy St Petersburg bonds, they won't invest, and we run the risk that our debut will turn out to be a failure," Artemyev said.
"Because of this we have slowed our work down a little to wait for definite information and to receive the documents we need from the Federal Tax Service and Finance Ministry."
President Boris Yeltsin signed the bill introducing the tax on Wednesday, but it will only come into effect when it has been officially published.
In the meantime many details of the tax, including exactly what is taxable and who is liable, remain unclear.
Federal government officials and deputies agreed during work on the tax that Russia's own sovereign Eurobond, issued last November, would not be liable to the tax.
Artemyev said officials from international rating agencies would visit St Petersburg in early February to give it a credit rating.
